contract_plain_english: For any two real numbers a and b, their product is at most one half of a squared plus one half of b squared.

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Lemma 2.7.7, sentence introducing the elementary Young inequality
source_evidence.observation: The source states ab <= a^2/2 + b^2/2 for a,b in R.

source_evidence.anchor: First inequality in the proof of Lemma 2.7.7 after display (2.22)
source_evidence.observation: The inequality is applied pointwise to bound |XY| by X^2/2 + Y^2/2 inside the exponential.

definitions_and_conventions: The square and order are the ordinary real square and order.
implicit_context: This is a deterministic real inequality; it does not require probabilistic assumptions.

details: Both variables range over all real numbers.
The product is bounded above by the arithmetic mean of the two squares.

undebatable_constraints: The domain is all a,b in R.
The left-hand side is ab, with no absolute value in the displayed Young inequality itself.
The right-hand side is exactly a^2/2 + b^2/2.
